# Format datetime columns to desired string format
def format_datetime(series):
    # Format as day-month(abbr)-year hour:minute:second
    # Use .dt.strftime('%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%S') but with month capitalized properly
    # pandas strftime uses locale, but we can ensure first letter capitalized
    formatted = series.dt.strftime('%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%S')
    # Capitalize month (b gives abbreviated month with first letter capitalized in English locale)
    # Actually %b gives "May", "Jun" etc already capitalized in English locale
    # However, we need to ensure NaN stays NaN
    formatted = formatted.where(series.notna(), pd.NA)
    return formatted
